perf.summary: The trial-division loop guard 'p*p <= n' recomputes a multiply every iteration; n is invariant so iterate while p <= isqrt(n) or compare against a hoisted limit.
perf.currentCost: One 64-bit multiply per loop iteration just for the bound check, plus the % p each step. For prime n this loop runs ~sqrt(n)/2 times, so the multiply is on the critical path of every iteration.
perf.proposedChange: Compute the bound once: 'long limit = (long)System.Math.Sqrt(n);' guard 'while (p <= limit)' with a final correction (limit*limit may be off-by-one due to FP), or keep p*p but note the multiply. Alternatively hoist by maintaining 'pSq += 4*p+4' incrementally? Simpler: precompute limit via integer sqrt to drop the per-iteration multiply.
perf.rationale: Replaces a per-iteration 64-bit multiply with a single sqrt + a cheap p<=limit compare, cutting the dominant per-iteration cost for the common prime/hard-to-factor case.
perf.risk: FP sqrt can be off by one near perfect squares; must clamp limit (e.g. while((limit+1)*(limit+1)<=n) limit++; while(limit*limit>n) limit--;) to stay exact. If exactness is hard to guarantee under Burst's fast-math, keep p*p<=n — flag as optional. Semantics must remain identical for all n.
